articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

However, in its November 4 order, the Supreme Court concurred with the need for optimum utilisation of mineral resources but left the decision on transferring mining rights to the State government’s discretion, rather than making it mandatory.

articles.title: Nabeel Rajab, prominent Bahraini human rights activist, dies at 62
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Nabeel Rajab, a prominent democracy activist in Bahrain who helped lead the island nation's 2011 protests known across the wider region as the Arab Spring and who spent years in prison for challenging its monarchy, died on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). He was 62.

His family found him unresponsive at their home in Turkey on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) morning, activists said. The Bahrain Center for Human Rights, which Rajab once led as president, confirmed his death in a post on X.

"We extend our sincere condolences and heartfelt sympathy to his esteemed family. We pray that God may encompass him with his vast mercy and reward him abundantly for his efforts and contributions," the group wrote.

Ebrahim Sharif, an activist who was a close friend of the family, said Rajab's wife and daughter found him unresponsive early in the morning at their home in Turkey. He said he had spoken to Rajab's brother and that the family believed Rajab likely died of a heart attack.

Rajab left Bahrain early in the Iran war, as authorities cracked down on Shia-led protests throughout the Gulf island kingdom, home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet. Rajab accused the government of torturing an imprisoned activist and feared he would be arrested if he returned, he told The Associated Press at the time.

Rajab rose to international prominence in 2011, as the Arab Spring uprising swept the region and demonstrations erupted in Bahrain's capital, Manama. He was a pivotal figure in the protest movement, during which the country's majority Shiite population demanded the ruling Sunni monarchy offer them greater political freedoms. As president of the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights, he advocated for expanding the powers of Bahrain's parliament, ensuring freedom of expression and fighting anti-Shia discrimination.
Bahraini authorities, backed by Saudi troops, arrested scores of demonstrators and crushed the protests, while ultimately introducing limited political reforms.

He was imprisoned on multiple occasions in the years following the unrest. His longest stretch behind bars began in June 2016. He was eventually released in June of 2020 during the coronavirus pandemic, though he was ordered to spend the remaining time in home detention.

At the time, he had been serving a five-year sentence over tweets criticising the Saudi-led war in Yemen and alleging prison abuse. He had also been sentenced to two years over comments deemed critical of Bahrain.

Rajab had a history of heart issues. During one of his earlier detentions, he received treatment for an irregular heartbeat. He separately received a pardon from King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa in 2015, after concerns emerged about Rajab's health.

articles.title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U krainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), calling it an "unprecedented" operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.

Mr. Zelenskyy portrayed the operation on the Kerch Bridge as a masterstroke, as Ukrainian forces gradually wore down Russian air defenses for weeks before bombarding the prized target with a barrage of missiles and drones overnight.

Mr. Zelenskyy didn't detail the damage, but the Ukrainian General Staff said an arch and a span of the bridge's road section collapsed, severing the road link, while the railway line was still standing but its arch was damaged.

The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and to support troops on the front line. The construction of the bridge, a potent symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of the peninsula in 2014, was inflammatory for Ukrainians.
"The symbol of the occupation has cracked," the Ukrainian General Staff said in a statement.
Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, hitting two of the Ukrainian capital's main bridges and killing at least two people.

A recent escalation in aerial attacks came as Russia and Ukraine await a date for the next round of U.S.-mediated talks aimed at ending the war that began with Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbour on February 24, 2022.

U.S. President Donald Trump says he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week.
The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Mr. Zelenskyy said on social media.
Ukrainian forces knocked out defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said.

Domestically developed long-range drones struck the bridge's road section during the night while Ukraine's Neptune missiles and other drones aimed at the rail section, he said. Flamingo precision-guided missiles delivered the final blow, he said.
Russia's Investigative Committee said the bridge was attacked by drones and sustained damage. It didn't elaborate.

articles.title: Iran targets Bahrain, slams 'fabricated' dirty-bomb report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Iran launched a fresh drone attack against Bahrain on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and dismissed a report alleging a dirty-bomb plot against the United States, which President Donald Trump said he took "very seriously".

Mediator Qatar urged "all parties" to show restraint following an uptick in hostilities, with Bahrain targeted three times in five days after a lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf countries since September.

Mr. Trump was speaking after CNN cited seven anonymous U.S. officials as saying Iran was plotting to target senior administration figures with a "dirty" bomb, laced with chemical or radioactive materials.
"If there is [such a threat], they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before," Trump said after arriving for a summit in the Philippines.
"I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy."
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei dismissed the report as "fabricated".

"Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations" including "the fabricated media narrative surrounding an alleged 'dirty bomb' propagated by CNN", he posted on X.
Mr. Baqaei also criticised a New York Times report questioning whether Iranian dams and water projects had military uses.
Earlier on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), explosions boomed across Bahrain's capital as a mobile-phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

Bahrain's armed forces said they "confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today... before they could achieve their objectives", while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S.-operated radar system.

"Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.

The attack was in response to the "repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones", it added. The Guards also said they had intercepted and captured a US drone south of Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant to national grid
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant at Rooppur in the country's northwest Pabna district began supplying electricity to the national grid on a trial basis on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), according to officials.
The 2,400 MW Russian-assisted facility is expected to meet more than 10% of Bangladesh's electricity demand once fully operational, helping the country diversify its energy sources.
“We have become the 33rd country in the world to produce and generate nuclear power,” Science and Technology Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam told reporters at the plant site.
The development comes as the South Asian nation of 170 million people grapples with a fuel crisis triggered by the conflict in West Asia.
The plant comprises two units, each with a generation capacity of 1,200 MW, officials said, adding that the first unit has begun supplying 350 MW of electricity to the national grid.

According to the Science and Technology Ministry, the initial connection would last between eight and 10 hours, during which engineers would conduct tests on the plant's turbine, generator and grid stability.
The unit would subsequently be disconnected for further technical tests and could be reconnected after about 28 hours for another four to six hours to complete additional operational checks.
Under an agreement with the Russian contractor, the first unit will undergo a 10-month trial operation before beginning commercial electricity generation at full capacity, the ministry said.
Construction on the facility began in 2017 during the administration of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, following a 2015 agreement with Moscow.

articles.title: India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that India or any other country could not dictate terms over deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s return home.

"Neither India nor any other country can dictate terms on this,” Mr. Zahed said during a media briefing when asked for comments on a media report saying New Delhi had hinted at two conditions for handing over Hasina.
Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government.
Talking to reporters at the Bangladesh Secretariat, Mr. Zahed said, “Bangladesh is now an independent, sovereign state standing on firm legal ground and it will reject any unjust terms.”
The premier’s Adviser, however, said he did not believe India would attach conditions to returning Hasina.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Hasina's extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.
He further said: “India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh."
Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal convicted Hasina in November 2025 of crimes against humanity for her role in the crackdown on protesters during the July-August 2024 uprising.
Tried in absentia, she was sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Hasina has rejected the charges and the proceedings.

In a report last week, BBC Bangla said unnamed Indian officials indicated that New Delhi set two main conditions to facilitate Hasina’s return amid Dhaka’s repeated insistence on her extradition under a bilateral treaty despite her repeated stated plan to return home voluntarily to face the legal procedure.
The report said that “under the conditions, India wanted Bangladesh Army to directly receive Hasina either via a military flight to Delhi or at a land border crossing”.
It said New Delhi simultaneously demanded judicial safeguards on her return, seeking assurances that she would receive the right to appeal her death penalty and undergo a fresh trial.

articles.title: ‘Record horticultural production’ shows increase of 4.36% from 2024-25: Agriculture Ministry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: India’s total horticultural production is expected to reach 3,869.15 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 161.77 lakh tonnes (4.36%) over the production recorded in 2024-25, according to the third advanced estimates of area and production of horticultural crops released by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan in New Delhi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). In the previous crop season, horticulture production stood at 3,707.38 lakh tonnes.

Mr. Chouhan expressed satisfaction over the projected growth and said the significant increase in horticultural production reflected the hard work of India’s farmers and the impact of the Union government’s farmer-friendly policies. “This record production would not only strengthen the country’s nutritional security but also directly contribute to higher incomes for horticulture farmers,” the Minister said, congratulating farmers across the country for their efforts.

Farmers were increasingly moving beyond traditional crops towards the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, and plantation crops, including cashew, coconut and cocoa, as well as aromatic and medicinal plants, he said.

“This growing interest in commercial and high-value crops is opening up new avenues of income for farmers while creating fresh opportunities for self-reliance and growth in the agricultural sector,” Mr. Chouhan said, adding that one of the most significant aspects of the latest estimates was increase in production despite a reduction in the area under horticultural cultivation.

“The total area under horticultural crops in 2025-26 is estimated at approximately 297.21 lakh hectares, compared with 301.36 lakh hectares in 2024-25. Despite the decline in cultivated area, production is projected to increase across fruits, vegetables, flowers, plantation crops, and aromatic and medicinal plants,” Mr. Chouhan said.

Fruit production is estimated to rise from 1,176.49 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 1,230.66 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 54.18 lakh tonnes or 4.60%. “The improved output is primarily attributed to better production of banana, mango, papaya, apple, pomegranate and jackfruit,” the Union Agriculture Ministry said in a release.

The area under vegetables is estimated to increase from 117.91 lakh hectares to 119.31 lakh hectares. “Vegetable production is projected to rise by 4.35%, from 2,177.97 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 2,272.68 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. The increase is primarily driven by higher production of potato, tomato, brinjal, bottle gourd, cucumber, cabbage, beans and peas,” the release added. Potato and tomato production are both expected to register strong growth. Potato production is estimated at 655.70 lakh tonnes, up 11.95% from 585.71 lakh tonnes in the previous year. Tomato production is projected to increase from 205.99 lakh tonnes to 214.11 lakh tonnes. Onion production is estimated at 288.96 lakh tonnes.

Flower production is projected to rise by approximately 14.45%, from 42.65 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 48.82 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. “The area under flower cultivation has also increased to 4.10 lakh hectares,” it added. In the production of plantation crops, including arecanut, coconut, cashew, betel leaves and cocoa. “Their combined production is estimated to increase by 7.56% to 182.64 lakh tonnes. Production of aromatic and medicinal plants is also expected to rise from 9.01 lakh tonnes to 9.28 lakh tonnes,” the Ministry of Agriculture added.

The production of turmeric, garlic, curry leaves and cardamom is also expected to grow. “The total area under spices in 2025-26 is estimated at 47.56 lakh hectares, with production projected at 123.54 lakh tonnes,” the Ministry said.

articles.title: Hospital in Chennai performs complex aortic surgery on 10-year-old boy with rare vascular disease
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A 10-year-old with a rare inflammatory blood vessel disease underwent surgery at SIMS Hospital, Chennai, to repair a large aneurysm of the aortic arch, the hospital said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The patient was diagnosed with aortoarteritis, also known as Takayasu arteritis, a condition that causes inflammation and narrowing or enlargement of blood vessels. The aneurysm had enlarged significantly, causing breathing difficulty, palpitations, and difficulty lying down. The risk of rupture made urgent surgery necessary. The patient weighed about 18 kg, adding to the technical challenges of the operation. As the aneurysm was located close to the breastbone, opening the chest through the usual approach carried a risk of injuring the enlarged aorta. The surgical team first connected the patient to a heart-lung machine through blood vessels in the groin.

The patient’s body was cooled to 16°C using a technique known as deep hypothermic circulatory arrest. Blood circulation was then temporarily stopped for about 40 minutes, enabling surgeons to remove the affected section of the aorta and replace it with a Dacron graft. Lowering the body temperature reduces metabolic activity and the organs’ oxygen requirements, helping protect them during the period when blood flow is interrupted.

The patient was subsequently rewarmed, restoring his blood circulation. Post-operative assessments showed no damage to the brain, kidneys, intestines, or spinal cord, the hospital said. The patient has resumed normal activities without breathing difficulty but will require continued medication and monitoring to control the underlying inflammation and prevent further aneurysms.

The surgery was performed by a team led by Bashi V. Velayudhan, director and senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, along with Mohammed Idhrees, senior consultant, cardiothoracic surgery, and a team of anaesthesiologists and other specialists.

articles.title: Chinese scientist fired after child death in gene-editing trial: state media
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A Chinese scientist who concealed the death of a six-year-old girl in a gene-editing trial has been sacked following a government probe, according to state media.
The girl died last year after receiving experimental gene therapy to correct a non-life-threatening condition -- which was not disclosed in published research, an investigation found in July.

Neuroscientist Zilong Qiu, the trial's lead researcher, had made no mention of the girl in a paper published in the prestigious journal Nature , according to the joint investigation by Science and Retraction Watch .

Qiu was dismissed as deputy director of the Songjiang Research Institute affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, state broadcaster CCTV said Friday, citing a statement from Shanghai authorities.
The reported statement included only Qiu's surname, but referenced the Nature study published on February 18.
Qiu was given a five-year suspension from participating in scientific projects and recorded in a database for "serious breaches of research integrity", the report said.
Another researcher on Qiu's team was sacked and handed a five-year suspension, while several others with ties to the hospital where the trial took place were also punished.
The child who died had a rare neurodevelopmental condition called Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome, according to the report.
The hospital's ethics committee had approved a gene-editing trial to treat the disorder in January 2025, the report said.
The committee terminated the study after the girl died in March due to complications from gene therapy.
Shanghai authorities found that Qiu's team failed to properly inform the hospital of possible safety issues from earlier tests on primates, according to the report.
The July investigation by Science and Retraction Watch found that the girl's parents, who paid more than $800,000 to fund the experiment, were not adequately informed about the risks.

articles.title: Microplastics, 'cocktail' of hazardous chemicals in Delhi's Yamuna, flags study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Microplastics in the Yamuna in Delhi are accompanied by a complex mixture of organic chemicals, including pharmaceutical residues, pesticides and industrial effluents, with many of these substances classified as human-health and environmental hazards, according to a new study by University of Delhi researchers.

The study, published in the 'Journal of Hazardous Materials Advances ' in September 2026, examines microplastic pollution and associated chemical profiles at eight locations along a 48.8-km stretch of the river in Delhi -- from its entry at Palla to its exit at Asgarpur Jagir -- highlighting how pollution patterns vary across agricultural, residential, industrial, recreational and forested areas.

Researchers recovered 2,289 microplastic particles from the samples, with an average abundance of 3.18 particles per litre. The analysis identified 321 distinct chemical compounds across the samples, of which 50 were detected in extracts of recovered microplastic fractions at four or more locations.

Of these 50 compounds, 36 corresponded to structures with Global Harmonized System (GHS) hazard classifications, covering categories such as carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, acute toxicity and aquatic hazards.
Seven compounds were detected across all eight sampling locations, including 2-naphthylamine, lidocaine and monobutyl phthalate, the study found.
The researchers also identified pharmaceutical compounds such as atomoxetine, domperidone and telmisartan, along with agrochemical-related substances, including diuron and thiamethoxam.

Radhey Shyam Sharma, head of the Department of Environmental Studies at University of Delhi and one of the co-authors of the study, said the findings highlight the need to look beyond microplastic particles and examine the complex chemical mixtures present in river ecosystems.

"The microplastics problem, along with this cocktail of organic and inorganic substances, needs to be looked at through the lens of mixture toxicity. The land-use pattern has also been explored in the study," Sharma said.
He stressed the importance of nature-based solutions, including strengthening vegetation along riverbanks and protecting natural river ecosystems, to minimise pollution-related risks.

"Vegetation ecosystems can help prevent pollution from entering the river. Natural ecosystems and riverbanks need to be strengthened to minimise these risks. The focus should be on nature-based solutions," he said.

The study found significant variations in microplastic abundance across the eight locations. The highest concentration was recorded at the recreational-hydraulic site near the barrage, followed by a floodplain area where multiple drains converge.
The lowest abundance was recorded at the agricultural entry point at Palla and a forested stretch of the river.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time improves an already perfect classic
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Remakes of past games are pure genius. There are several titles that were mega hits in the 90s or early 2000s when both silicon and game engines were breaking new ground in 3D. Many of those games do not hold up today as well as the pixel game era of the NES and SNES eras do.

Capcom has shown the world that remaking most of their lineup of Resident Evils has been successful. Ubisoft did it too, with Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag Resynced . No one expected Nintendo to jump into the fray, but they did and with style, not only remaking a Zelda game, but one of the cult favorites from the Nintendo 64 era. A game so loved, that it is continuously ranked as one of the greatest games of all times, which is a risky move to remake.
Fortunately, the Ocarina of Time remake not only wears that crown proudly, but is also the only game this year to challenge the sales might of the neon clad tsunami that is Grand Theft Auto VI .

Another saga begins in the cyclic battle of good versus evil, and it revolves around the only boy in the village without a fairy. Entrusted with the fate of the world Link must stop the evil Ganondorf who is intent on grabbing the Tri-force — an artefact that grants the bearer immense power. Guided by the enigmatic fairy Navi, Link must leave the safety of his home, Kokiri Forest, and journey across the sprawling expanse of Hyrule Field, venturing through perilous dungeons, and shift between childhood and adulthood to claim the Master Sword and become the Hero of Time.

Jumping between time from Link’s adult self to his child form is so meta, it will make you feel like you too are jumping through time with him. As an adult, tethered by responsibilities of adulting, you get to jump back to your childhood — something that is more poignant than nostalgia.

In comparison to some of the more sweeping, complex narratives of today’s fantasy games, Ocarina of Time harks back to a simplistic form of storytelling, which was mostly due to cartridge size restrictions. However, it is a template that many of Zelda’s best games have been set on. First-time players are sure to find Link’s story a refreshing one that focuses on core gameplay mechanics and a beautiful reimagining of the world.

The world is gorgeous and while it is not quite open, it does feel like it has got a lot of freedom of movement. It is great to explore all the temples filled with its well-created puzzles that you may remember the solutions for and see the new renditions of iconic places such as Death Mountain, Hyrule Field, Temple of Time and other faithful to their original designs, but are now a lot more fleshed out.
Much of the world has a lot more detail. So rather than rushing through the game, take in your surroundings and scrutinise houses, because there is environmental storytelling peppered everywhere.

Much of the game has been faithfully translated, but thankfully it is free from the oddities of that N64 controller. In addition to updated control mechanics, there are a lot of quality of life improvements, and those who have played Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom , may find the controls familiar. The motions are fluid, and there are some physics-based systems at play, that make everything from the sword clashes feel solid to the sensation of things being physically there in the world as they bounce around.

Combat gains quality of life improvements, inheriting motion aiming from its predecessors making it more snappy, lively and reactive. It lets you acrobatically dodge, backflip and attack enemies, and hits do feel like they actually connect. The enemy AI and animations have been changed to make those fights all the more nail-biting. This being the Switch 2, there are also motion controls to help you use Hookshot, Longshots, bows for some more dynamic ranged combat, if you preferred using this in the newer Zelda games. The addition of jump mechanics do change the dungeons a bit, meaning instead of having the original jump in certain zones, now you actually have to platform across.

As any Anime fan will tell you, to never venture into the English dubs, because many of them feature some over-the-top voice work. The only nitpick with Ocarina of Time is the voice acting features common thick American accents that are found in those same Anime dubs, that completely feel out of place.

I wish Nintendo had chosen a more neutral accent or even gibberish blips to pass for a more Hyrulic language. The sound design on the whole is great though, especially the music, which features a orchestral rendition of Koji Kendo’s unforgettable score. The best part is is the unlimited fun gamers can have making music on the Ocarina.

articles.title: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. articles.title: Brace for impact: On rising inflation and external factors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment.

Further, there is strong evidence to suggest that the official inflation metrics are not capturing the full extent of rising prices. Data on cash with the public and UPI transactions show the value of both has been growing in double digits over the last year and more, significantly outpacing nominal GDP growth. This either suggests that the informal economy is far larger than earlier thought or, more likely, that inflation is well above what the official figures are being able to capture. Unfortunately, there are no real magic-wand fixes to this situation. Inflation is largely beyond the government’s control, and wage growth cannot happen overnight. The only way forward is to continue trying to spur sector-specific growth and warn people of the impending storm.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: Karnataka to send letter to Centre on excessive ethanol blending on November 17
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State Government will write to the Centre on Tuesday (November 17) detailing the results of tests on ethanol content in the petrol dispensed at fuel outlets in Karnataka, said Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Rizwan Arshad.

Speaking on the sidelines of a programme organised at the Dasara Exhibition grounds in Mysuru to inaugurate the Food and Civil Supplies Department stall on Sunday (November 15) evening, Mr. Arshad said the letter would also include a set of measures needed to address the issues while also outlining the measures the State government proposed to take if the Union government failed to act.
The letter will also point out how oil marketing companies tried to dodge the issue in their replies, the hardships faced by consumers and the evidence gathered by the State government.
He said the entire process of fuel dispensation lacks transparency, with neither the quality nor the quantity of petrol supplied to consumers being ensured.

The laboratory tests conducted by the State government have revealed excessive ethanol blending, with levels varying up to 30% and, in certain cases, as low as 13%, despite the Union government’s claim that the E20 blending process is controlled and automated, he said.
“Common people are paying more for substandard fuel. If the Union government fails to act, we will take measures within our power to safeguard the interests of the public,” the Minister stated.

Pointing to the lobby backing ethanol blending, Mr. Rizwan said the Union government’s policy was aimed at encouraging ethanol production. The country was producing more ethanol than could be blended with petrol. The government was caught between the interests of ethanol manufacturers and other stakeholders, he said.
He also pointed out that vehicle engines were not designed to support higher levels of ethanol blending with petrol.

Citing the findings of a survey, the Minister said that 85% of petrol bunks in the State were allegedly not dispensing the correct quantity of fuel for the amount paid by consumers. Of the nearly 3,200 dispensing nozzles tested, 2,700 were found to have errors. Similarly, 762 of the 805 petrol bunks surveyed were found to have discrepancies, he said.

articles.title: 50 gold medals awarded at VSKU convocation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Vijayanagara Sri Krishnadevaraya University (VSKU) has recorded an overall pass percentage of 95.33 in its examinations for the academic year 2024-25, with 42 students securing 50 gold medals at its 14th annual convocation on Monday.
Also, the university presented rank certificates to 137 students, 66 undergraduate and 71 postgraduate.

Among postgraduate students, Savita of Sri Guru Thipperudra College in Ballari topped the list with four gold medals in Commerce followed by R. Tasmiya Banu of the VSKU main campus secured three gold medals in Industrial Chemistry.

Four studentsUjjani Eshwar (Physics), Samreen (Chemistry), Padmavathi K. (Social Work), all from the university’s main campus, and Mahalingappa Tambralli (History and Archaeology) from the Postgraduate Centre, Nandihalli, have won two gold medals each.

In the undergraduate category, the gold medal winners include Pooja (B.Com) of BBC College, Ballari, Ajay (B.Sc) of GVP Government First Grade College, Hagaribommanahalli, Basamma (BA) of Jnana Bharathi Degree College, Ballari, and B. Kavya (BSW) of Gangotri Degree College, Kottur.
As many as 13,346 undergraduate students and 1,448 postgraduate and diploma students have cleared the examinations, contributing to the overall pass percentage.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi unveils her memoir Belonging - A Journey of Love with Rahul, Priyanka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) chairperson Sonia Gandhi formally launched her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love , with Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi by her side on Monday (November 16, 2026).
“Response to the book has been overwhelming, I’m deeply touched,” said Sonia Gandhi during the book launch event.
‘Belonging’ means ‘you belong’; when you’re an outsider, you feel not being liked & always watched, Sonia Gandhi added on the book title.

Several INDIA bloc leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and TMC’s Abhishek Banerjee, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and BJP leader Amarinder Singh attended the launch of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Published by HarperCollins India, Belonging: A Journey of Love was released last Tuesday (November 10, 2026) to a lot of enthusiasm from readers, who have been lining up at prominent bookstores to pick up copies of the memoir while many have been ordering it online.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former party chief Rahul Gandhi and AICC general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were present at the official launch event at the ITC Maurya.

Other than Mr. Vijay, Akhilesh Yadav and Mr. Banerjee, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, J&K Chief Minister Omar Obdullah, National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah, NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule, BJP leader and ex-Punjab Chief Minister Amarinder Singh, Congress chief ministers D. K. Shivakumar (Karnataka) and Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu (Himachal Pradesh) also attended the launch event, along with several senior Congress leaders.

VIDEO | Delhi: Explaining why she decided to write her memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi says much has been written about her family, including her mother-in-law, husband, son, daughter and herself, but most of it is far removed from reality. "Stories are woven around you. Untruths are woven around you, hurtful things are said which are nowhere near the truth. And I thought, well, perhaps this is a way of bringing out my feelings, what I know of my family, and maybe people will be sort of open to listen to my story too," she said.

articles.title: Mettupalayam-Coonoor-Ooty Road likely to be restored by November 20
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Traffic on the Mettupalayam — Coonoor Road is likely to resume in the coming days, with officials from the National Highways wing stating that the road could be reopened to traffic as early as this Friday (November 20).

The officials overseeing the repair works along the Coonoor ghat said the rain in October had triggered 19 landslips within the Nilgiris district, while five landslips had occurred in Coimbatore. Out of 19 landslips in the Nilgiris, only three were major and they have largely been cleared.

Work is in progress to clear the major landslip sites in Coimbatore. An official coordinating the repair works along the Coimbatore section said they have tentatively marked the road to be reopened, at least partially to traffic, by November 20.

The landslips have caused huge disruptions to the Nilgiris’ economy, with the price of vegetables and essential commodities increasing due to higher transportation costs. Travel to Coonoor and Udhagamandalam from Mettupalayam has been rerouted through Kotagiri, with many local residents complaining of long traffic jams. The road closure has also reportedly affected tourist inflow into the district, with many potential visitors discouraged from travelling to the district due to the closure of the Mettupalayam — Coonoor Road.

articles.title: Kumara Krupa Guest House now turned into Chief Minister’s official residence, renamed ‘Ganga’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The old Kumara Krupa Guest House in Bengaluru has now been converted into the Chief Minister’s official residence and has been renamed “Ganga”. In a private ceremony on Monday, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar performed puja at the new residence and also announced that all the legislators and MPs will be invited on Thursday to the new residence.
The Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms (DPAR) issued a notification on Monday, renaming the old guest house “Ganga” and declaring it as the Chief Minister’s official residence.
The Chief Minister said he had chosen to relocate to the Kumara Krupa Guest House as the quarters sanctioned to him were small and the Kumara Krupa Guest House was not being used.
A view of Kumara Krupa Guest House in Bengaluru. | Photo Credit: File Photo

The Chief Minister said the old building had been slightly renovated without altering its heritage value, denying allegations to the contrary. He maintained that Opposition leaders would be able to verify the same when he invites them to the programme on Thursday.

Referring to the curiosity and concerns regarding the cost of renovation, he said efforts had been made to minimise the cost, including using inexpensive marble and Kota stone for the flooring. Old furniture from the guest house had been used, while furniture from his own house too had been brought to avoid buying new furniture, he explained. To a query on the total cost of the renovation, the Chief Minister said he was yet to receive the bill.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.
Similarly, the crude petroleum and natural gas segment saw inflation climb to 70.8% in October 2026 from 57.3% in September. This was compared to a 7.2% contraction in prices in October of last year.

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

However, in its November 4 order, the Supreme Court concurred with the need for optimum utilisation of mineral resources but left the decision on transferring mining rights to the State government’s discretion, rather than making it mandatory.

articles.title: Equity vs bonds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Diversification may have its virtues but so does concentrated investments. Sector funds are examples of concentrated bets. In this article, we draw a distinction between concentrated bets in the equity and the bond markets and show why the former is meaningful and the latter, somewhat risky.

In theory, equity has unlimited upside potential. That means stock prices can rise to any level. In the real world, stock prices have high, not unlimited, upside potential given our finite investment horizon. Yet, concentrated bets can be meaningful. If you expect the banking sector to do well in the coming year, buying units of a banking sector ETF or a sector fund could be optimal. But the downside can be high if your bet turns wrong.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: COP31 draft deal calls for ‘accelerated action’ to exit fossil fuels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: COP31 co-host Australia released the first draft of a broad political deal on Monday (November 16, 2026) that includes a call for nations to speed up the phaseout of planet-heating coal, oil and gas.
The draft decision needs ultimate approval by nearly 200 nations at the UN climate summit in Turkiye where the future of fossil fuels has been among the most heated issues.
The proposed agreement lays out the competing positions of governments in Antalya and underscores how far apart they remain with a consensus deal due by Friday.
The draft "calls for accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels, including through the immediate transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems".

It also evokes "deep concern" over the impending breach of the Paris accord's 1.5C target and recognises the "central role of the best-available science" of the IPCC, the global authority on climate change.
Many countries, particularly in Europe and climate-vulnerable developing nations, have pushed for a reference to the IPCC and urged a faster exit from fossil fuels in the final text.
The text also calls for a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to reach at least $120 billion, a key demand of these nations.
Australia, which is steering the marathon talks, wants to produce an overarching political statement summing up what countries have agreed in Antalya and setting the course for future climate action.
The summit, which closes on November 20, takes place against a difficult backdrop, with a conflict-driven energy crisis and geopolitical tensions tempering expectations.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.
Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.

“We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death,” she said ‌in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

Deborah Bergamini, national deputy secretary of the Forza Italia party, on Sunday criticised Giacomo Filibeck, Secretary General of the Party of European Socialists, for his comments at the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad.

On Saturday (November 14, 2026), Mr. Filibeck had expressed support for Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi's campaign against alleged irregularities in the country’s electoral rolls and used the slogan "Vote Chor Gaddi Chhod," a Hindi political slogan that translates as “Those who stole the vote must vacate their seats”.

VIDEO | Hyderabad: At the Bharat Summit, Secretary General of the Party of European Socialists, Giacomo Filibeck said, "Rahul Gandhi has defended a simple principle on which every democracy rests; 'one person, one vote'. His campaign for clean and transparent voter rolls and the thousands who marched with him to Ramlila Maidan just two weeks ago remind us that democracy is not given. It is defended by people willing to stand up for it. 'Vote Chor Gaddi Chhod'. The Congress Party built the democratic foundation of modern India." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)

In a social media post, Ms. Bergamini, without naming Mr. Filibeck, said an Italian representative of the European Socialist and Democratic Party had attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP at a meeting organised by the Indian National Congress (INC).
Ms. Bergamini’s party, Forza Italia, is part of Italy's ruling coalition, led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.
"I believe that in a democracy, everyone is free to raise the theses and accusations they believe. Provided they can prove them," Ms. Bergamini said.

She added that it was "inappropriate to enter into an internal political debate of a great friendly country", with which Italy had established a "special strategic partnership" and developed cooperation across sectors.
Ms. Bergamini also said Europeans should not give lessons on democracy to India, which has 970 million voters.
"India has its political institutions and its judiciary: any conflict and contestation must be resolved by following and respecting the rules of democracy," she said.
At the Bharat Summit, organised by the INC on November 13-14, Mr. Filibeck said Mr. Gandhi had defended the principle of "one person, one vote".

"His campaign for clean and transparent voter rolls and the thousands who marched with him to Ramlila Maidan just two weeks ago remind us that democracy is not given. It is defended by people willing to stand up for it," he said.

articles.title: Beijing hails ‘groundbreaking significance’ of U.S., China, Russia summit in Shenzhen
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Thursday’s (November 19, 2026) summit meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia will be “of groundbreaking significance”, Beijing said on Monday (November 16, 2026), hailing the symbolism of a meeting of the three leaders taking place in China.
China’s Foreign Ministry said President Xi Jinping will host the summit with President Donald Trump and President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

“The upcoming China-Russia-U.S. summit in Shenzhen will mark the first-ever face-to-face meeting among the heads of state of the three countries. The three leaders will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-country relations, and the meeting will be of groundbreaking significance,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said, adding that “strengthening communication, managing differences and stabilising relations among China, Russia and the U.S. serve the interests of all three countries”.

The meeting is likely to be more symbolic than substantial. U.S. officials have indicated that the agenda is the war in Ukraine, the situation in West Asia, including stabilising global energy supplies, and nuclear arms control. Whether there will be any concrete outcomes on any of those issues remains to be seen.

That has not, however, dampened enthusiasm in China, where state media has hailed the significance of the meeting. Beijing officially eschews references to a “G2” with the U.S. or a “G3” with the two countries and Russia, maintaining that it supports multipolarity. At the same time, the symbolism of China hosting the meeting has been seized upon to highlight Beijing’s global standing.

“The fact that China, Russia and the U.S. will sit down for face-to-face talks once again demonstrates that the head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance,” an editorial in the Global Times said. “The effort to foster a new type of major-country relationship marks a new phase in China’s major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics, featured by proactive leadership and systematic construction. The meeting to be held in Shenzhen is a manifestation of the international community’s high recognition of China’s image as a stable and responsible major country.”

Taking aim at naysayers, the editorial added that “those who view the trilateral meeting between China, Russia and the U.S. as major countries ‘carving out new spheres of influence’ or establishing a ‘new Yalta system’ clearly hold only a one-sided view of history, ignoring historical patterns.”

“They focus solely on the needs of individual parties while disregarding the overall and comprehensive interests, emphasise only the power aspect of major countries while neglecting their responsibilities, and are so preoccupied with the reality of polarisation in the international landscape that they lose sight of the ideal of democratising international relations,” it said.

Symbolism aside, few experts in China expect substantial outcomes amid what they acknowledge is growing strategic rivalry between China and the U.S. on the one hand, and an enduring rift between Russia and the West on the other, especially with the continuing war in Ukraine. Russia was “most enthusiastic” among the three for the summit, Su Liuqiang, a scholar at the Centre for American Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, said in an interview with state media last week, adding that an informal exchange was likelier than a more structured, formal trilateral summit.

“On the one hand, there is substantial political resistance in the U.S.,” he said. “Anti-Russia sentiment remains strong in both the U.S. and among its European allies, with opposition to negotiating with Moscow while bypassing Ukraine and Europe. On the other hand, the three countries have differing priorities; Russia’s core concern is negotiations on a ceasefire in Ukraine, the U.S. is interested in the Russia-Ukraine conflict and non-proliferation, China supports peace talks but must also balance its relations with the U.S., Russia, Europe and Ukraine. In this context, a low-profile trilateral meeting is the more realistic option,” he added, noting that practical outcomes could emphasise stabilising global energy supplies.

While China preferred “multilateralism” over ideas such as the G2 or a U.S.-China-Russia triumvirate, Mr. Su said a meeting would still be significant in suggesting that while structural competition between big powers would still continue to define global geopolitics, there was increasing interest in “managing that competition and preventing it from escalating or spinning out of control.”
